candidates: Name private, transitional, or internal base classes with a leading underscore (e.g., `_LimitedAtoms`) to clearly signal they are not part of the public API. Avoid names such as `BaseAtoms` that imply the class is designed to be subclassed by external users.

When refactoring a public class to use a private internal base class, keep the comprehensive user-facing docstring on the public subclass rather than moving it to the private base. The private base class's docstring should only describe its internal or transitional role.
Do not mention private or internal implementation classes (those prefixed with an underscore) in changelog entries. Changelogs should document only user-facing API additions, changes, and removals.

Methods that have been through the full deprecation cycle (`DeprecationWarning` followed by `FutureWarning` across multiple releases) are suitable candidates for removal during a refactoring MR. When removing such methods, include a clear, prominent announcement in the release notes rather than relying solely on the code diff or inline deprecation messages.
